issues.description: The UML in the problem statement names Ride's second attribute 'abbreviation' (char), but the solution (and thus the intended API students will observe) uses the field name 'shortName' and exposes it via getShortName(). This naming difference between the specification (abbreviation) and implementation (shortName / getShortName) can confuse students about the expected attribute/getter name and may cause mismatches with tests or their own implementations if they follow the UML literal names.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the naming consistent between the UML/problem statement and the code. Either (A) change the UML and problem text to use 'shortName' (and document the getter getShortName()), or (B) rename the field and getter in the code to match the UML: use a field named 'abbreviation' (char) and a getter getAbbreviation(). Ensuring the attribute and getter names match the specification will avoid student confusion and test mismatches.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines the Ride attribute as 'abbreviation: char' (and therefore students will expect a corresponding field/getter named abbreviation/getAbbreviation). The provided solution, however, names the Ride attribute 'shortName' with getter getShortName(), while some subclasses (e.g., RollerCoaster, LaunchedDropdownTower) use the parameter name 'abbreviation' in constructors. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual attribute (the character that abbreviates a ride) across the problem statement and the solution creates mapping friction for students: they must mentally reconcile 'abbreviation' from the UML with 'shortName' in the code, and may be uncertain which identifier to use when implementing or when the exercise tests expect a specific name.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename the Ride field and its getter in the solution from 'shortName' / getShortName() to 'abbreviation' / getAbbreviation() (and update constructor parameter names accordingly), or (B) update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' so all artifacts share the same name. Option (A) is recommended because it preserves the UML wording and avoids student confusion when mapping the diagram to code.
